title: main-sync git-merge-main uses --no-ff so a diverged branch can sync

sha_binding.verified_source_note: Last commit on this branch touching a non-proof path. merge_sha is null pre-merge as the shared evidence contract requires (CEP-E7); it is bound to the real merge commit by post-merge-lane-close.yml.

verdict.statement: git-merge-main built `git merge --ff-only origin/main`, which cannot merge a diverged branch by definition, so main-sync's recommended exit for divergence failed on exactly the condition it exists for -- leaving git-rebase-main, which rewrites history and invalidates every head-pinned governance artifact, as the only operable path. The command is now `git merge --no-ff origin/main`, which merges a genuinely diverged branch while preserving both sides' commit SHAs byte-for-byte, and which is deliberately not a bare `git merge` because that would fast-forward a merely-behind branch and make the verb's effect depend on divergence state. All five wrapper safety invariants live outside buildExtendedCommand and are structurally unaffected.

No package.json, lockfile, tsconfig or build-config change. No workflow, branch-protection, proof-schema or bypass-flag change.
Four --ff-only occurrences belonging to main-sync's legitimate `git pull --ff-only origin main` were deliberately left unchanged.
known_gaps: A merge that conflicts still requires manual resolution by the operator; the wrapper reports it actionably and releases the mutex but does not resolve it.

A --no-ff merge advances the branch head by one merge commit, which still moves the PR head SHA and therefore still invalidates head-pinned governance artifacts. This lane makes the sanctioned exit operable and SHA-preserving for existing commits; it does not eliminate re-authorization after a sync.
